Koden Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kodeń, Poland

Demolished. Kodeń's Jewish cemetery, likely established soon after the town's founding in 1511, has its earliest recorded mention in an act of violence: the destruction of its tombstones in riots in 1698 — a notably early instance of anti-Jewish vandalism, predating the more commonly documented 20th-century destructions elsewhere in this collection by over two centuries. In 1941, the Germans completely destroyed the cemetery and used its tombstones to pave the road to Piszczac; Kodeń's Jews were transported to Międzyrzec Podlaski, documented elsewhere in this collection, and then to Treblinka the following year.
